body:
The parent issue with description is #2690 

Proposed level changes for requirement in chapter "V4 Access Control"

Full list of requirements for the chapter is listed here: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x12-V4-Access-Control.md

| # | Description | Level change |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **4.1.8** | [ADDED] Verify that adaptive security controls related to authentication and authorization decisions based on a consumer's environmental and contextual attributes (such as time of day, location, IP address, or device) are implemented as defined in access control documentation. | 2 > 3 |
| **4.2.4** | [ADDED] Verify that changes to values on which access control decisions are made are applied immediately. Where changes cannot be applied immediately, (such as when relying on data in self-contained tokens), there must be mitigating controls to alert when a consumer performs an action when they should no longer be able to do so and revert the change. Note that this would be unable to mitigate information leakage. | 2 > 3 |
| **4.3.4** | [ADDED] Verify that multi-tenant applications use cross-tenant controls to ensure consumer operations will never affect tenants with which they do not have permissions to interact. | 1 > 2 |

comments.body:
4.3.4 is a super-important control for access control. I would keep it at level 1. When its a problem it's usually a very easy way to steal a massive amount of data.

| # | Description | Level change |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **4.3.4** | [ADDED] Verify that multi-tenant applications use cross-tenant controls to ensure consumer operations will never affect tenants with which they do not have permissions to interact. | 1 |

4.3.4 is edge-case or just an extra outcome as an impact for 4.1.3 and 4.1.6 and those are Level 1. You can not have 4.3.4 without 4.1.3 and/or 4.1.6

* V4.1.3	Verify that the application ensures that function-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions.
* V4.1.6 Verify that the application ensures that data-specific access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific data items to mitigate insecure direct object reference (IDOR) and broken object level authorization (BOLA).

I think "you can not have 4.3.4 without 4.1.3 and/or 4.1.6" is a very fair comment, Elar.

But when 4.3.4 is in play, it's a very easy attack that allows for mass data theft of a large number of users. This seems to fit your L1 definition very well. But if you (fairly) think this is just an offshoot of 4.1.3/4.1.6 then should we remove 4.3.4 and and merge it into the others somehow?

> This seems to fit your L1 definition very well.

I still don't think we should start talking about multi-tenant for L1.

>  But if you (fairly) think this is just an offshoot of 4.1.3/4.1.6 then should we remove 4.3.4 and and merge it into the others somehow?

This has been my message entire time for the requirement. If you want to re-open this discussion, it makes sense to search and re-open some related issues where it went through long journey already. I prefer to keep this issue for level changes only.

I remember that discussion well. I see your point a bit more clearly.

I think 4.3.4 is very important but it might not need to be a separate requirement. I'll open a new issue to consider moving 4.3.4 into 4.1.3/4.1.6.
See https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2716 for the continued conversation on this.
4.3.4 got it's own discussion, for level changes there seems to be agreement for now. So I'll PR it in.
